title: Budget-aware prefill orchestrator and quantization hint adapter
author: Sofia Patel
release_notes: Adds a tenant-budget-aware prefill orchestrator with a quantization hint adapter; includes new telemetry and a canary rollout. No API breaking changes; safe fallback to existing profiles enabled.
description:
Problem: production customers running mixed workloads were seeing unpredictable token-unit economics because prefill choices (when to prefill KV/cache and how much) were independent of tenant budget profiles and quantization compatibility heuristics. This PR introduces a budget-aware orchestration layer that ties prefill aggressiveness to tenant budget tiers and a lightweight quantization hint adapter that signals conservative/experimental quant profiles to serving nodes.

What this changes: 1) new orchestration service component (prefill/orchestrator) that consumes tenant budget metadata and runtime latency SLOs and produces prefill decisions (none/minimal/aggressive) as a short-lived decision token; 2) quantization hint adapter that annotates requests with a per-tenant model-compat hint (e.g., q4_0_safe, q4_1_gain) so runtime can choose an appropriate kernel path and fall back automatically; 3) telemetry hooks (metrics and events) covering decisions, estimator confidence, budget consumption, and fallback counts; 4) an operator-configurable policy file and a canary rollout that targets 5% then 25% then 100% of tenants; 5) unit + integration tests and a synthetic workload harness used in CI.

Motivation: automating sensible defaults for prefill and quantization reduces manual tuning, protects tenants on tight budgets from aggressive prefill/cost regressions, and enables the runtime to pick quant paths with graceful degradation. This complements the existing econ prescriptor work by providing a runtime-facing decision token that is cheap to evaluate and transparent in telemetry.

Design notes: - Decisions are intentionally stateless and short-lived; they can be recomputed from tenant metadata and recent SLO telemetry. - The quant hint adapter does not change model artifact files or perform quantization in-line; it only annotates requests so the serving runtime can select prebuilt variants. - Safety gate: when the runtime detects >5% mismatch error rate for a quant hint, it will automatically downgrade to the safe profile for that tenant for 1 hour and emit an alert.

Testing and rollout: - Unit tests for policy parsing, decision logic, and hint format. - Integration test harness simulating mixed chat/embedding load with synthetic sequences to validate budget churn and fallback behavior. - Canary rollout script and config added to tooling so SRE can advance percentage in a controlled rollout.

Backward compatibility and migration: - No customer-facing API changes. - New small DB table (prefill_profiles) added via migration script; existing tenants get a default conservative profile. Migration script is included and idempotent.

Commits summary: - "init: budget-aware prefill orchestrator skeleton" - "impl: decision token format and policy parser" - "feat: quantization hint adapter and request annotation" - "telemetry: add metrics for decision count, fallback count, budget spend" - "tests: add unit & integration harness" - "docs: operator playbook and rollout guidance" - "ci: add synthetic workload job and canary gating"

Changed files (high level): server/prefill/orchestrator.go, server/prefill/decision_token.proto, server/quant/hint_adapter.py, api/tenant_profiles/migrations/20241112_add_prefill_profiles.sql, telemetry/metrics_registry.yaml, tooling/canary/rollout_playbook.md, tests/prefill/integration/harness.go, docs/operators/prefill-and-quant-playbook.md, examples/tenant_profiles/sample_policy.yaml, ci/workflows/prefill-canary.yml, scripts/migrate_prefill_profiles.sh, webapp/admin/prefill_overview.ui.tsx

Notes for reviewers: - Focus review on the policy parser (edge cases where overlapping rules apply) and on the quant hint wireformat compatibility with existing runtime headers. - Pay special attention to the migration script for idempotency on retry.

References: Linear ENG-2561, design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2561/budget-aware-prefill, and internal RFC (rfc/prefill-budget-2024-10.md).

Sofia Patel: Updated tests to assert on correctness and budget consumption rather than strict latency, added a separate perf smoke test that runs nightly.
Marco Rivera: Telemetry names look fine, but suggest prefixing prefill metrics with 'prefill.' to make them easy to locate in dashboards.
